messages.content:
The writer's note about it, in their words: A post on Xiaohongshu after my weekend in Hangzhou.
A learner of Simplified Chinese (as used in mainland China) is rewriting part of a post for Xiaohongshu (travel post):
<<<
大家好！我是美国人，在上海学中文已经一年了。上个周末我和朋友去杭州玩，在西湖边一走就是三个小时，风景美得让人舍不得停下来。

但是我有一个问题：我在一个饭馆点了西湖醋鱼，服务员说这个菜很有名，可是我觉得它太酸了，我不是很喜欢吃。是不是我点得不对？还有什么杭州菜你们推荐我试一试吗？谢谢！
>>>
The part: "我有一个问题"
What is wrong with it: Here 有一个问题 announces a real difficulty, and Chinese readers expect the writer to say what went wrong, such as bad service, a bad dish or a bad experience. The post then asks only whether the writer ordered the wrong thing, so the frame promises more than the question delivers.
What they mean (confirmed by them): Only a question about my own taste and order.
A version that works (never show it or any stretch of it): "我有个问题想请教大家"
Words they already have as hints: 请教, 问问, 疑问, 大家
They are stuck. Write two hints that help them build it themselves, never giving them the wording:
- plan: in English, one or two short sentences, as their tutor: how a fluent writer builds this part: what comes first, what follows, how the parts connect (contrast, cause, addition) and where the emphasis goes. Name no Simplified Chinese (as used in mainland China) word except the hint words above (none from the working version), no letter counts, no fill-in blanks. It is about the words of this part, never the content they talk about ("first the interactions between them, then…" plans a story, not the sentence). When the part is a word or two (left in English, or a missing word), say what kind of word goes there and how it sits in the sentence.
- example: one short Simplified Chinese (as used in mainland China) sentence a fluent writer would actually write (grammatical and natural on its own), about an everyday topic unrelated to the post (different people, things and events), built the same way as the working version: the same pattern and the same connecting words, none of its other content words. Put [square brackets] around the few words it shares with the working version as they are (the frame they can borrow, at most four), never around the words that change.
The writer may write to you in any language; whatever they write in, everything you write for them is in English.
Reply with JSON only: {"plan":"","example":""}

result.text: {"plan":"Open by stating that you have one small matter, then follow with a clause saying what you want from readers, so the frame signals a polite request rather than a complaint. Put the verb for asking for advice just before the word for the audience, so the sentence ends by addressing everyone and the tone stays light.","example":"[我有个]好消息[想]告诉[大家]。"}
